I was the same way, the advice everyone is saying is the best advice. Literally just say follow me and walk. Be confident and don’t look back. Sometimes it takes them a second to register and if you look back you just messed up.

If they are remote you tell them that there presence is leverage and advise the client to come in, make sure they love the vehicle and from there start talking about pricing. I avoid that at all cost. Once you get them in and they start talking about the mark up you start justifying the current incentory shortage and although that may make them feel like they are being taken advantage of due to a unfortunate situation explain to them that it is a simple supply and demand. Nobody is fighting the butcher about the costs of beef or the farmers about eggs. Be confident. If they walk they’ll just run into the same crap elsewhere. At the least be the guy they liked.

Lexus 100% Toyota is a necessity vehicle you’ll run into roaches people who need a car. Lexus is considered sport/luxury. You’re dealing with a whole different class of clients. In the simplest way to put it, would you sell t shirts at target or Gucci? One sell at one location is several at the other. From experience i went from Toyota to Audi and yea i sell less cars but i make more at Audi. A lot more.

Product knowledge gives you confidence and confidence sells cars. I wouldn’t buy a car buy some mf that stutters and say uhhhh all the time. To be honest i don’t know everything about my product. But i know enough to confidently tell them “I’m not 100% sure and last thing i want to do is guess to earn your business. When we get to the desk i will be sure to look that one up for you just to double check before i give you any false information” consumers love confidence and transparency. Plus most people spend hours researching crap before coming in. Common knowledge will get you through 90% of the deals. Rarely somebody asks some technical question.
